newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bond yields close lower as currency strengthens.
newsitem.headline: NZ bond yields close lower as currency strengthens.

text.p: New Zealand bond yields were encouraged lower on Thursday by strength in the U.S. market.
Bank bills fell a point as the New Zealand currency firmed on strong rumours of another $100 million samurai issue.

The December futures rose four points to 90.61 while the physical market remained heavy, weighed down by high cash, the imminent October 12 general election, and the Reserve Bank's desire to maintain tight conditions.
Borrowing demand in the middle of the curve saw yields rise and further distorted its shape.
Dealers said GDP data on Friday morning will be keenly watched to see if it gives the Reserve Bank more evidence of a slowing economy and a reason to ease monetary policy.
A poll of 10 economists forecast seasonally adjusted GDP would rise a seasonally adjusted 0.4 percent in the June quarter for an actual rise of 2.3 percent in the June year.
Anything higher would see the 90-day bank bills rise as an easing is put further into the distance.

Today's $50 million indexed bond tender was well received with dealers suggesting investors were onto a winner whatever the outcome of the election. The status quo would see bonds rally and the indexed bonds would be unaffected by higher inflation introduced by a left-of-centre government.
